page-title.purpose: One per screen, at the top, ink. 26px/600 with balanced wrapping.

section-title.purpose: Card groups and settings sections, 19px/600, 24px above.

body.purpose: Instructions and prose on UI pages, 16px/1.5, capped at 68ch.

label.purpose: Buttons, field labels, list-row primary text. 14px/600 sentence case.

meta.purpose: Author, chapter count, timestamps, hints. 12px muted ink.

reading-body.purpose: The book itself. Literata 17px/1.7 at a 66ch measure; only place the serif is allowed.

shadows.name: raise
shadows.purpose: Resting chip, sticky bar top edge. Dark: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.4).

shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Menus and popovers anchored above content.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions (colour, background, border).

motion.name: dur-2
motion.purpose: Progress fill width, small layout shifts.

motion.name: dur-3
motion.purpose: Sheet and panel entrance. Nothing in the system is longer.

breakpoints.name: rail
breakpoints.purpose: Bottom bar becomes an 88px left rail; --nav-h drops to 0.

darkTheme.note: Dark mode is a second complete token set under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark), not an inversion.

focus.purpose: One ring for the whole product. Never the browser default, never red, never a shadow.

touchTargets.note: Chips are 36px unless they are filters on touch, then .chip-tap raises them to 44px.

narrative.overview:
PharmaReader is a desk, not an app store product. Paper underneath, ink on top, one lamp. A resident opens it at 11pm with a chapter they have already read twice and a viva on Thursday; nothing on screen competes with the paragraph in front of them. The surface is warm paper, text is near-black ink with a green cast, and the only saturated colour on most screens is the teal of an action the reader actually chose.

The system is two-faced in one body. UI chrome is the platform's own sans, because a study tool shouldn't cost a font download to say "Import". Long-form text is Literata, self-hosted so the reader works with the network off. The two never mix inside one sentence; the boundary is exactly the boundary between this app and the book.

Depth is nearly absent. Paper does not float. Shadows appear only where a thing genuinely leaves the page, and hierarchy comes from size, weight, colour temperature and hairline rules. The mood is quiet clinical competence: the tool of someone precise who does not need to impress you.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, ink text, one teal voice per screen.
Flat surfaces; hairline rules instead of shadows; depth reserved for sheets.
Sans for chrome, Literata for text — never both in one block.
4px spacing rhythm, 44px minimum touch target, generous tap padding on phones.
Complete light and dark themes; both are first-class, not an inverted afterthought.
Motion is 120–240ms, eased, and always skippable via prefers-reduced-motion.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Teal is the reader's voice, not decoration. One teal element per screen region: the primary action, or the active nav item, or the current selection. If two things are teal and only one can be pressed, the other is wrong. Headings are ink, never teal.

rules.name: The Paper Not Glass Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are opaque paper. No translucency, no backdrop blur, no gradients behind text. A surface earns its edge from a one-step lighter fill and a hairline, not from a glow.

rules.name: The Ink On Tint Rule
rules.body: Semantic colour is applied as text/icon on a wash, never as a wash on a wash. A warning banner is warning-coloured text on a warning wash; it is never a saturated amber slab with white text.

rules.name: The Native Chrome Rule
rules.body: UI text is the platform's sans at a fixed rem scale. No web font is loaded to render "Import". If a glyph is missing, the platform's fallback is correct by definition.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Literata appears only inside reading content. It never appears in a button, label, banner, nav item, or heading. A serif button is a costume.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Reading text stops at 66ch, UI prose at 68ch, regardless of how wide the window is. On a 1280px screen the column is centred and the margin is the point.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Shadows are for things that float over content, not for things that sit in it. If a shadow is doing the work a hairline could do, remove the shadow.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: No backdrop-filter, no semi-transparent surfaces, no frosted panels. The one translucency in the system is the sheet's scrim, and that is a scrim, not a surface.

dos: Do keep one teal action per screen region and let headings stay ink (One Voice Rule).
Do reach for a hairline or a one-step tonal shift before reaching for a shadow.
Do give every tappable thing 44px of height and, on touch, 48px for the primary.
Do use rem for type and spacing so 200% text zoom reflows instead of clipping.
Do put a leading 18px icon in ghost buttons that toggle a panel; bare ghost text reads as a link.
Do pair a progress bar with its numeric value, and show no bar at all when a book is unstarted.
Do write empty states that teach the next action and name the constraint.
Do check both themes at 390px before calling a screen done; dark is not an afterthought.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion — the global block already collapses all animation to 0.01ms.
donts: Don't use teal for headings, decoration, or two competing actions on one screen.
Don't add a coloured border-left stripe to cards, callouts, or banners — status is the fill plus the icon.
Don't use glass, blur, translucency, or gradient text anywhere.
Don't put a kicker/eyebrow line above a heading; the heading is enough.
Don't use clamp() type scales for product UI; the scale is fixed rem steps (11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 19, 22, 26, 32).
Don't use Literata for UI chrome, or a display face anywhere (Two Voices Rule).
Don't stack cards inside cards, or give a card a shadow to separate it from paper.
Don't use emoji, icon fonts, or filled icon styles as interface icons.
Don't animate longer than 240ms or bounce; a page turn is the reference motion.
Don't let body text run wider than 68ch just because the window is wide.
